doc_friction.issue: Default base fails on the shallow clone ('no merge base'); --base HEAD~1 works. The error message says so, but a fresh cloud session always hits it.

Step 0 says take the top unclaimed alert, but the top ~10 were already triaged as false positives in docs/reports/2026-11-25-security-queue-false-positives.md; the queue has no way to mark triaged alerts until the owner dismisses them (PR #18809 proposes one).
--history and --park need ventures/<v>/ to exist; payapps lives only in private-monorepo, so the tool's own suggested fix fails with 'No venture folder' and only --replace works.

deviations.why: Claim branches (security-fix/code-scanning-<n>) conflict with the session's harness rule to push only to its assigned branch.
deviations.did: Worked on the assigned branch; the PR title names the alerts so other sessions see the claim through PR search.
deviations.result: Duplicated: PR #18837 (another session) fixed the same two alerts at the same time. No claim branch from either session, so neither could see the other. The claim-branch convention is what prevents this; a session barred from pushing other branches should search open PRs by alert number right before starting, and again before merging.

deviations.why: prompt.md step 0 puts the security queue before routing; the run's budget went to it, not to the ventures focus.
deviations.did: Fixed two alerts and triaged the remaining queue.
deviations.result: Every alert in the 48-alert queue now has a reading on file.

deviations.why: No new post or agent doc: the only surviving change is a test fix with no reader audience.

notes: The security fixes (#849, #65) and the third-pass triage were duplicated by PR #18837, which merged while this PR's CI ran; the flagships payapps trim was also made on main. After merging main those changes dropped out (main's versions kept). What this PR still lands: platform/distribution/homebrew.test.mjs's command-line test preloads a fetch stub that answers 404, so it no longer calls registry.npmjs.org. That test failed this PR's changed-ventures job once (8 tests, 1 fail; passed locally and on rerun), and runHomebrew throws on any registry status other than 200/404, so an npm 429 or refused connection fails it. Verified: node --test platform/distribution/homebrew.test.mjs 8/8.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: read and triage ~20 alerts, two small fixes with a test

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
